title: [Bug] Dynamic LoRA loading is effectively unsupported with --tokenizer-worker-num > 1 (per-worker registry, no cross-worker sync)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Dynamic LoRA adapter operations (`/load_lora_adapter`, `/unload_lora_adapter`, and the `from_tensors` / `from_distributed` variants) only mutate the LoRA registry of whichever tokenizer worker process happens to serve the HTTP request. With `--tokenizer-worker-num > 1` there is no cross-worker synchronization of that state, so a dynamically loaded adapter is only usable by requests that happen to be routed to the worker that served the load. This is neither guarded nor documented today — it fails per-request, depending on connection routing.

Note this is **not** specific to any single endpoint: it is a property of the tokenizer-side control-plane state model. Adapters passed at startup via `--lora-paths` are unaffected (every worker seeds them at init).

**Mechanism (code references, current main):**

- Each tokenizer worker process constructs its own `LoRARegistry` and `lora_ref_cache`, seeded only from startup `--lora-paths` (`python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py`, `init_lora`: `self.lora_registry = LoRARegistry(self.server_args.lora_paths)`; `lora_ref_cache` is seeded from the same list).
- The dynamic load/unload handlers register/unregister only in the serving worker's registry (registration is deferred until backend success, then applied to that process's `lora_registry` / `lora_ref_cache`).
- `MultiTokenizerRouter` broadcasts only pause/continue to the workers ("Also broadcasts pause/continue to all tokenizer managers for consistent is_pause state" — `multi_tokenizer_mixin.py`); no LoRA state is synced.
- Generate requests resolve `lora_path -> lora_id` against the **local** worker's registry (`tokenizer_manager.py`: `obj.lora_id = await self.lora_registry.acquire(obj.lora_path)`), preceded by a hard error when the name is not in the local `lora_ref_cache`: `"Got LoRA adapter that has never been loaded: {lora_path}"`.

**Expected behavior — one of:**

1. **Guard**: reject dynamic LoRA endpoints when `tokenizer_worker_num > 1` with an explicit error — matching what #30913 now does for the `upsert` flag specifically (`_validate_lora_upsert_supported`).
2. **Document**: state in the LoRA docs / server-args docs that dynamic loading requires `--tokenizer-worker-num 1`.
3. **Support it properly** (larger project): either replicate registry mutations across workers via the `MultiTokenizerRouter` broadcast path (needs centralized `lora_id` minting, an ack barrier before the load returns 200, partial-failure semantics, and a story for per-worker LRU/eviction divergence under `--max-loaded-loras`), or move `lora_name -> lora_id` resolution to a single authority (scheduler side), so tokenizer workers stop holding load-bearing dynamic state.

Happy to contribute option 1 or 2 as a small PR if maintainers agree on the direction.

### Reproduction

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct \
  --enable-lora --max-loras-per-batch 4 \
  --tokenizer-worker-num 2
```

1. `POST /load_lora_adapter` for adapter `X` → lands on worker A → 200.
2. Send `/generate` requests with `lora_path=X` from fresh connections → requests landing on worker B fail with `"Got LoRA adapter that has never been loaded: X"`, requests landing on worker A succeed. Failure rate ≈ (N-1)/N, routing-dependent.
3. Re-`POST /load_lora_adapter` for `X` (e.g. as a "retry") → if it lands on worker B, a fresh `lora_id` is minted and the scheduler-side duplicate-name check fails with `"already loaded"` — confusing, because from the client's view the adapter both "doesn't exist" (step 2) and "already exists" (step 3).

### Environment

Established by code inspection on current `main` (874fc07d9); the mechanism is version-independent — the per-worker `LoRARegistry` / `lora_ref_cache` construction and the local-only resolution path are visible at the references above. Originally observed while reviewing the RL multi-LoRA flow in #30912 / #30913; it predates those PRs.
